steps.title: The weekend problem
steps.say: Every hot weekend, the cold drinks aisle is empty by noon. The nightly forecast only sees it the next morning, when the sales are already lost.
steps.caption: Empty by noon, seen the next morning

steps.title: Sales as they happen
steps.say: Here is store 112, live. Every sale lands in a Confluent topic the moment it rings up.
steps.caption: Every sale lands in Confluent as it rings up

steps.title: A forecast in the stream
steps.say: IBM Granite forecasts the next day for this store, right inside Confluent. No training and no model per store, just the next 24 hours with its range.
steps.caption: The next day, zero-shot, inside Confluent

steps.title: The weather changes the plan
steps.say: Then the weather stream says 36 degrees by noon. The same model reads it, and the afternoon forecast climbs right away.
steps.caption: A heat wave lifts the afternoon forecast

steps.title: The shelf goes quiet
steps.say: Just before noon, sales stop for 40 minutes. That is not a slow hour. It is an empty shelf, and it is flagged as it happens.
steps.caption: Forty quiet minutes, flagged as an empty shelf

steps.title: The order moves first
steps.say: So the next truck grows by 204 cases before the two o'clock cutoff, and the shelf stays full through Sunday.
steps.caption: The next truck grows before the cutoff

steps.title: Where it runs
steps.say: All of it runs where the data already flows. Sales and weather topics feed Flink, Granite forecasts each store, and the order goes straight to replenishment. The usual way copies, retrains and scores overnight, a day too late.
steps.caption: In the stream, not in a nightly batch

steps.title: What changes
steps.say: Fewer stockouts on hot weekends, orders that move in minutes, and one model for every product in every store.
steps.caption: Fewer stockouts, faster orders, one model

spec.title: Card testing held before authorization
spec.subtitle: Every authorization scored against the card's own normal, inside the stream.
spec.pain: Card testing slips through as small charges, and the big fraud lands before the batch rules catch up.
spec.outcome: Testing is held within seconds, and real customers pay without friction.

context.name: Customer history
context.event: Same cards seen at 9 new merchants in 2 minutes

anomaly.label: Card testing: 3× small attempts in 2 min

decision.action: Hold the next authorizations on this card range
decision.impact: Testing stopped before the large purchase

usual_way.steps: Static rules, then a batch model on settled transactions

kpis.label: from first test charge to a hold

steps.title: Small charges, big losses
steps.say: Card testing starts with tiny charges. By the time batch rules catch it, the large purchase has already cleared.
steps.caption: Tiny charges first, the big loss after

steps.title: Every authorization
steps.say: Every authorization on this card range streams into a governed Confluent topic, with its schema checked on the way in.
steps.caption: Every authorization, governed and live

steps.title: The expected band
steps.say: TSPulse, from the IBM Granite family, learns nothing per card. It reads the stream zero-shot and draws the expected band for the next minutes.
steps.caption: An expected band, zero-shot, for every card range

steps.title: The burst
steps.say: Then three times the usual small attempts arrive in two minutes. The anomaly score jumps outside the band, on the event itself.
steps.caption: Three times the attempts, scored as they land

steps.title: Hold, not decline
steps.say: The next authorizations on that range are held within two seconds, so the testing stops before the large purchase, and travelers elsewhere still get through.
steps.caption: Held in two seconds, travelers still pass

steps.title: How it runs
steps.say: In Flink SQL, one call to the anomaly detection function scores each window as it arrives. The result lands in a topic that the authorization service reads. Nothing is copied out, and there is no model to train.
steps.caption: One Flink SQL call, results back in a topic

steps.title: What changes
steps.say: Holds in seconds, fewer false declines, and no models to train or retrain.
steps.caption: Seconds to hold, fewer false declines
